excerpt: Sharing a nice analysis by Opus that I agree with. I'm sympathetic to the user experience sucking in this situation and I am busy filing an issue that would end up fixing this. 🤖 Note the title is backwards: per the description, it's {{q.op=AND}} that fails and {{OR}} that works. The problem is where the tag is placed. In {noformat} fq={!tag=collapse_tag}{!collapse field=someid} {noformat} the leading local-params n…

"q.alt" then becomes technically "alt" when viewed by the query parser of "q", due to the hoisting I proposed. For consistency anyway, not because I think the parameter deserves it otherwise. I don't love that change specifically but why not. If I might take this local-param hoisting farther a little, I'd make "q.type" be a preferred substitute for "defType" since "type" happens to be the little-known local-param th…

A different path that would be less controversial is to drop the hoisting idea, but nonetheless still transition to local-param only for certain important parameters -- namely transition "q.op" and "df", to local-param only "op" and "f". This would let us use the DeprecationLog to warn users of legacy request parameters, whereas hoisting wouldn't.
